## Claims
- [proved] The supplied provider query set is exactly `persisted:source-39,source-29,source-30`; it contains none of `Smith normal form`, `determinantal divisors`, `unimodular minors`, or `Pieri matrices`. Hence the required targeted search was not executed.
- [source-backed] RWY prove integral generation of \(J_v\subset\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) by two Schur-interval families, using Pieri identities and induction; no stated Smith-form or unimodular-minor certificate occurs in the inspected result. [doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 864-892; 1009-1041; 1068-1142]
- [source-backed] St. Dizier–Yong use LR-coefficient linear equations and a terminating coproduct-tensor algorithm, not degreewise integer Pieri matrices or Smith/determinantal-divisor certificates. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 263-304; 494-516; 598-632]

## Strategy
For the current objects, \(\overline\Lambda=\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\), with
\[
I_{r,n-r}=\operatorname{Span}_{\mathbb Z}\{s_\lambda:\lambda\nsubseteq(n-r)^r\},
\quad
\bar s_\mu\bar s_{(k)}
=\sum_{\nu\subseteq(n-r)^r}c_{\mu,(k)}^\nu\bar s_\nu.
\]
A degree-\((d,k)\) Pieri matrix would have entries \(c_{\mu,(k)}^\nu\), for \(|\mu|=d\), \(|\nu|=d+k\). No inspected candidate states a determinant, unit minor, determinantal divisor, or Smith diagonal for such a matrix.

The exact search-audit certificate is established: the provider ran only the three persisted-source queries above, not the required targeted queries. The requested targeted literature search itself is **not established**.
